# Introduction

Supplement to the paper "Confidence intervals for the F1-score in medical object
detection: comparing bootstrap and Bayesian multilevel methods".

Code and data: <https://github.com/ndevln/f1-score-ci-object-detection> (data: `S1_Data_Pathologists.csv`, `S2_Data_MIDOG_Models.csv`).

The Bayesian binomial + Poisson models of Example 1 (pathologists vs ML model) and
Example 2 (MIDOG challenge) use the brms default priors. This script refits all models
with two alternative prior sets and compares the marginal pooled and grouped
F1-scores (median and 95% QI, computed as in the examples).

| Prior set | Intercepts | SDs (image, pathologist) | Correlation (pathologist) | Domain effects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| default | brms default: student_t(3, $\mu$, 2.5) | half-student_t(3, 0, 2.5) | lkj(1) | flat |
| tight | normal(0, 1.5) | half-normal(0, 1) | lkj(2) | normal(0, 1) |
| wide | normal(0, 10) | half-student_t(3, 0, 10) | lkj(1) | normal(0, 10) |

The intercepts are on the logit scale (recall) and the log scale (FP count per
image). The location $\mu$ of the default intercept prior is 0 for the recall part and
the log median FP count for the FP part.

Models (8 models x 3 prior sets = 24 fits):

- Example 1: pathologist model (image and pathologist effects) and ML model.
- Example 2, Part A: the three ML models (image effects).
- Example 2, Part B: the three ML models with Domain as a fixed effect.

All fits use 4 chains with 1000 warmup and 4000 iterations (12,000 draws). The fits
are saved in `fits_04/` and loaded on the next run (`brm(file = ...)`), so only the
first run takes long (about 1-1.5 hours, mainly compiling the 24 Stan models).

# Setup
## Load Packages
```{r}
# Seed (Article number of the Bertram et al. paper, as in Example 1)
set.seed(211067478)

# Data manipulation and visualisation
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggdist)

# Bayesian packages
library(brms)       # Fits the multilevel models via Stan
library(tidybayes)  # median_qi()/epred_draws() helpers for posterior summaries
```

## Functions
The F1-score from the counts (paper eq. 3), as in the examples:
$$F_1 = \frac{2\,TP}{P + TP + FP}, \qquad P = TP + FN$$

`format_result()` prints a point estimate with its interval as "0.68 (0.67 - 0.70)".
```{r}
calc_F1_score <- function(TP, FP, P) {
  2 * TP / (P + TP + FP)
}

format_result <- function(value, .lower, .upper) {
  fmt <- scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.01, trim = F)
  glue::glue("{fmt(value)} ({fmt(.lower)} - {fmt(.upper)})")
}
```

A prior set as brms priors. Every model only gets the priors of its parameters
(brms rejects priors for parameters that are not in the model): the correlation only
in the pathologist model, the domain effects only in the domain models. The default
set returns `NULL`, i.e. the brms default priors.
```{r}
make_priors <- function(intercept, sd, cor, b, rater, domain) {
  if (is.na(intercept)) return(NULL)
  priors <- set_prior(intercept, class = "Intercept", resp = c("TP", "FP")) +
    set_prior(sd, class = "sd", resp = c("TP", "FP"))
  if (rater) priors <- priors + set_prior(cor, class = "cor")
  if (domain) priors <- priors + set_prior(b, class = "b", resp = c("TP", "FP"))
  priors
}
```

Marginal pooled and grouped F1-score per posterior draw, as in the examples:
expected counts of every image in `newdata` (with the fitted image effects; new
pathologists get effects drawn from the fitted distribution), Bayesian bootstrap
weights over the images (shared by all pathologists of an image), then the median
and 95% QI. `by`: additional grouping, e.g. `"Domain"`.
```{r}
calc_marginal_F1 <- function(fit, newdata, by = character()) {
  epred_draws(fit, newdata = newdata |> mutate(GroundTruth = 1),
              allow_new_levels = TRUE, sample_new_levels = "gaussian") |>
    ungroup() |>
    select(.draw, all_of(by), any_of("rater_ID"), slide, P, .category, .epred) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = .category, values_from = .epred) |>
    mutate(TP = TP * P) |>   # TP part with trials = 1 is the recall
    # Bayesian bootstrap weights per image, shared by all pathologists of the image
    group_by(.draw, slide) |>
    mutate(weight = rexp(1)) |>
    group_by(.draw, across(all_of(by))) |>
    summarise(
      F1_pooled = calc_F1_score(sum(weight * TP), sum(weight * FP), sum(weight * P)),
      F1_grouped = weighted.mean(calc_F1_score(TP, FP, P), weight),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    pivot_longer(starts_with("F1_"), names_to = "averaging", names_prefix = "F1_") |>
    group_by(across(all_of(by)), averaging) |>
    median_qi(value) |>
    select(all_of(by), averaging, value, .lower, .upper)
}
```

## Load and Prepare Data
As in the examples. In Example 2 the images without objects (paper "Case A") are
excluded and the image column is renamed to `slide`, so both examples use the same
model formula.
```{r}
df_pathologists <- read_csv("S1_Data_Pathologists.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(rater_ID = as.factor(rater_ID), GroundTruth = TP + FN)

df_midog <- read_csv("S2_Data_MIDOG_Models.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(Domain = as.factor(Domain), GroundTruth = TP + FN) |>
  filter(GroundTruth > 0) |>
  rename(slide = Slide)
```

## Models
The three binomial + Poisson models of the examples:
```{r}
# Pathologist model (Example 1): image effects and correlated pathologist effects
bf_pathologists <-
  bf(TP | trials(GroundTruth) ~ 1 + (1|slide) + (1|r|rater_ID), family = binomial()) +
  bf(FP ~ 1 + (1|slide) + (1|r|rater_ID), family = poisson())

# ML model (Example 1 and Example 2, Part A): image effects
bf_ml <-
  bf(TP | trials(GroundTruth) ~ 1 + (1|slide), family = binomial()) +
  bf(FP ~ 1 + (1|slide), family = poisson())

# Domain model (Example 2, Part B): Domain as fixed effect and image effects
bf_domain <-
  bf(TP | trials(GroundTruth) ~ Domain + (1|slide), family = binomial()) +
  bf(FP ~ Domain + (1|slide), family = poisson())
```

The data of each model:
```{r}
df_ex1_pathologists <- filter(df_pathologists, model == "Pathologists")
df_ex1_ml           <- filter(df_pathologists, model == "ML-Model")
df_ex2_model_1      <- filter(df_midog, model == "Model 1")
df_ex2_model_2      <- filter(df_midog, model == "Model 2")
df_ex2_model_3      <- filter(df_midog, model == "Model 3")
```

The 8 models, each with its formula and data. `rater` and `domain` mark the models
with pathologist effects and domain effects (for the priors and the targets).
```{r}
tribble(
  ~example,    ~model,            ~formula,        ~data,               ~rater, ~domain,
  "Example 1", "Pathologists",    bf_pathologists, df_ex1_pathologists, TRUE,   FALSE,
  "Example 1", "ML model",        bf_ml,           df_ex1_ml,           FALSE,  FALSE,
  "Example 2", "Model 1",         bf_ml,           df_ex2_model_1,      FALSE,  FALSE,
  "Example 2", "Model 2",         bf_ml,           df_ex2_model_2,      FALSE,  FALSE,
  "Example 2", "Model 3",         bf_ml,           df_ex2_model_3,      FALSE,  FALSE,
  "Example 2", "Model 1, domain", bf_domain,       df_ex2_model_1,      FALSE,  TRUE,
  "Example 2", "Model 2, domain", bf_domain,       df_ex2_model_2,      FALSE,  TRUE,
  "Example 2", "Model 3, domain", bf_domain,       df_ex2_model_3,      FALSE,  TRUE
) -> df_models

df_models |> select(example, model, rater, domain)
```

# Prior sets
`NA` = brms default prior.
```{r}
tribble(
  ~prior_set, ~intercept,       ~sd,                   ~cor,     ~b,
  "default",  NA,               NA,                    NA,       NA,
  "tight",    "normal(0, 1.5)", "normal(0, 1)",        "lkj(2)", "normal(0, 1)",
  "wide",     "normal(0, 10)",  "student_t(3, 0, 10)", "lkj(1)", "normal(0, 10)"
) -> df_prior_sets

df_prior_sets
```

# Fit models
Every model with every prior set. The pathologist model uses the sampler settings of
Example 1 (`adapt_delta = 0.95`, `max_treedepth = 12`), the other models the brms
defaults. The fits are saved in `fits_04/` (`file_refit = "on_change"`: refit only if
the data, formula or priors change).
```{r}
dir.create("fits_04", showWarnings = FALSE)

df_models |>
  cross_join(df_prior_sets) |>
  mutate(
    fit = pmap(list(formula, data, rater, domain, intercept, sd, cor, b, model, prior_set),
               \(formula, data, rater, domain, intercept, sd, cor, b, model, prior_set)
      brm(formula,
          data = data,
          prior = make_priors(intercept, sd, cor, b, rater, domain),
          chains = 4, warmup = 1000, iter = 4000, cores = 4,
          control = if (rater) list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 12),
          seed = 211067478,
          refresh = 0, # No sampling progress in the output for PDF
          file = file.path("fits_04", paste(model, prior_set, sep = "_")),
          file_refit = "on_change")
    )
  ) -> df_fits
```

# Convergence
Max Rhat (should be < 1.01), min bulk and tail ESS (should be > 400) and the number of
divergent transitions (should be 0) per fit.
```{r}
df_fits |>
  mutate(diagnostics = map(fit, \(fit) {
    df_summary <- posterior::summarise_draws(as_draws_array(fit), "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail")
    tibble(
      max_rhat     = max(df_summary$rhat, na.rm = TRUE),
      min_ess_bulk = min(df_summary$ess_bulk, na.rm = TRUE),
      min_ess_tail = min(df_summary$ess_tail, na.rm = TRUE),
      divergences  = sum(subset(nuts_params(fit), Parameter == "divergent__")$Value)
    )
  })) |>
  select(example, model, prior_set, diagnostics) |>
  unnest(diagnostics)
```

# Marginal F1-scores
The targets of the examples:

- Example 1, pathologist model: average of the observed pathologists (their fitted
  effects) and single pathologist (one new pathologist, prediction interval).
- Example 1 ML model and Example 2, Part A: the observed images of the ML model.
- Example 2, Part B: per domain.
```{r}
df_fits |>
  mutate(estimates = pmap(list(fit, rater, domain), \(fit, rater, domain) {
    df_observed <- fit$data |> mutate(P = GroundTruth)
    bind_rows(
      calc_marginal_F1(fit, df_observed, by = if (domain) "Domain" else character()) |>
        mutate(target = if (rater) "average obs. pathologist" else "observed images"),
      if (rater) {
        calc_marginal_F1(fit, distinct(df_observed, slide, P) |>
                           mutate(rater_ID = "new_pathologist")) |>
          mutate(target = "single pathologist")
      }
    )
  })) |>
  select(example, model, domain, prior_set, estimates) |>
  unnest(estimates) |>
  # Short label for the tables and figures, e.g. "Ex. 1, average obs. pathologist"
  mutate(label = paste(sub("Example", "Ex.", example),
                       if_else(target == "observed images", model, target),
                       sep = ", ")) -> df_estimates
```

## Models without domains
```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Supplement Figure S4.1: Marginal F1-score (median and 95% QI) of the example models with the default, tight and wide prior set."
#| fig-height: 5
df_estimates |>
  filter(!domain) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = label, x = value, xmin = .lower, xmax = .upper, color = prior_set)) +
  geom_pointrange(position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), size = 0.2) +
  facet_wrap(~averaging, nrow = 1) +
  ggokabeito::scale_color_okabe_ito(name = "Prior set") +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "F1-score", breaks = (0:10) / 10) +
  ylab("") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

F1-score (median and 95% QI) per prior set:
```{r}
df_estimates |>
  filter(!domain) |>
  mutate(format = format_result(value, .lower, .upper)) |>
  select(label, averaging, prior_set, format) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = prior_set, values_from = format)
```

## Domain models
```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Supplement Figure S4.2: Marginal F1-score per domain (median and 95% QI) of the domain models with the default, tight and wide prior set."
#| fig-height: 6
df_estimates |>
  filter(domain) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = Domain, x = value, xmin = .lower, xmax = .upper, color = prior_set)) +
  geom_pointrange(position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), size = 0.15) +
  facet_grid(model ~ averaging) +
  ggokabeito::scale_color_okabe_ito(name = "Prior set") +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "F1-score", breaks = (0:5) / 5) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## Relative to the interval width
Change of the marginal F1-score with the tight and wide prior set compared with the default
priors, relative to the uncertainty of the default estimate. Domain models (at the bottom): the
largest change over the 10 domains.
```{r}
df_estimates |>
  mutate(width = .upper - .lower) |>
  group_by(label, Domain, averaging) |>
  mutate(
    shift        = 100 * abs(value - value[prior_set == "default"]) / width[prior_set == "default"],
    width_change = 100 * (width / width[prior_set == "default"] - 1)
  ) |>
  filter(prior_set != "default") |>
  # Domain models: the largest change over the domains
  group_by(domain, label, averaging, prior_set) |>
  summarise(
    shift        = max(shift),
    width_change = width_change[which.max(abs(width_change))],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(column = factor(paste0(if_else(averaging == "pooled", "Pooled", "Grouped"), ", ", prior_set),
                         levels = c("Pooled, tight", "Pooled, wide", "Grouped, tight", "Grouped, wide"))) |>
  arrange(domain, label) -> df_sensitivity
```

Shift of the median in % of the width of the default 95% QI (e.g. 5: the median moves by 5% of
the interval width):
```{r}
df_sensitivity |>
  mutate(shift = round(shift, 1)) |>
  select(label, column, shift) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = shift, names_sort = TRUE) |>
  rename(model = label)
```

Change of the width of the 95% QI in % (negative: narrower than with the default priors):
```{r}
df_sensitivity |>
  mutate(width_change = round(width_change, 1)) |>
  select(label, column, width_change) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = width_change, names_sort = TRUE) |>
  rename(model = label)
```
